bibliographic.title: PlayeRank: Data-driven Performance Evaluation and Player Ranking in Soccer via a Machine Learning Approach
bibliographic.venue: ACM Transactions on Intelligent Systems and Technology, 10(5):Article 59

scope.rationale: PlayeRank is a data-driven framework for multi-dimensional, role-aware evaluation and ranking of soccer players. It learns per-feature weights via a team-level classification task (LSVC predicting match outcome), then aggregates per-action contributions into a per-match player performance rating and role-based player rankings. Although it operates at the player/match level rather than the per-action probability level of VAEP/xT, it is an action-valuation framework: each event type/subtype/tag combination receives a weight that determines its contribution to player performance.

model.name: PlayeRank
inputs: event type, subtype, and tags (e.g. pass cross/simple, accurate/not accurate, key pass, assist, opportunity)
spatio-temporal coordinates (x,y) of each event used for role detection (player average position / centers of performance)
match outcome (win vs non-win) used as supervisory signal for feature weighting
76 features per player-match obtained by counting events of a given (type, subtype, tag) combination
model.target: Per-match player performance rating r(u,m) = (1/R) * sum_i w_i * x_i, where w_i are feature weights learned by a Linear SVM classifier trained to predict team match outcome (win = 1, non-win = 0) from the team's aggregated feature vector.
model.architecture: Three-phase pipeline: (1) Learning phase - Linear Support Vector Classifier (LSVC, L2-SVM via scikit-learn svm.LinearSVC) trained on team-aggregated feature vectors to predict match outcome, yielding feature weights w; k-means clustering (k=8) over players' centers of performance (average event positions) with soft-clustering (k-silhouette, delta_s=0.1) for hybrid roles. (2) Rating phase - per-player-match rating computed as scalar product r(u,m) = (1/R) * sum_i w_i * x_i; goal-adjusted rating r*(u,m) = alpha * norm_goals + (1-alpha) * r(u,m); series aggregation via Exponential Weighted Moving Average (EWMA). (3) Ranking phase - role-based rankings R_1,...,R_z assigning a player to role R_i if assigned to it in at least x=40% of matches.
model.spatial_resolution: Continuous (x,y) positions on a normalised 0-100 pitch; centers of performance computed as per-match average event coordinates and clustered into 8 roles; spatial query module uses a tessellation into 100 equal-sized zones (one per ~m^2 region, with note that solutions scale to ~10^6 zones if desired).
model.temporal_horizon: Per-match rating aggregates all events of player u in match m; player rating over series of matches uses EWMA across matches.

seasons: last four seasons (as of 2018) for club competitions; 3 seasons for Champions League and Europa League; 1 season for European Cup 2016 and World Cup 2018

metrics: AUC (Area Under the ROC Curve) of the LSVC classifier (AUC = 0.89)
Normalized Root-Mean-Square Error (NRMSE) between competition-specific and overall feature weights (avg ~6%)
silhouette score (ss = 0.43) for k-means clustering of roles at k=8
majority concordance c_maj with three professional scouts (overall 68%)
Pearson correlation between player average rating and standard deviation across roles
baselines: Flow Centrality (FC) by Duch et al. [12]
Pass Shot Value (PSV) by Brooks et al. [6]
random baseline classifier weighted by class frequencies (AUC=0.50, F1=0.53, accuracy=0.53)
evaluation.splits: 5-fold cross-validation for the LSVC feature-weighting classifier on 19,619 team-match examples (80% train / 20% test per fold). Splits are at the team-match level, not match level; the same match contributes two team-match rows (one per team) to the dataset, which could enable mild cross-team leakage within a match. Player rankings are evaluated against a survey of 211 player pairs judged by three Wyscout professional scouts.

claims.statement: PlayeRank achieves an improvement of up to 30% (relative) and 21% (absolute) with respect to the state-of-the-art Flow Centrality algorithm, and up to 16% (relative) and 13% (absolute) over PSV, on agreement with three professional Wyscout scouts.
The dataset comprises 31,496,332 events across 19,619 matches and 21,361 distinct players (21K reported in text) over four seasons of 18 prominent soccer competitions.
76 features (Table 7) were extracted per player-match, defined by combinations of event type, subtype, and tag (e.g. pass-simple pass-accurate, foul-hand foul-red card).

The Linear SVC trained to predict match outcome from team performance vectors achieves AUC = 0.89, F1 = 0.81, accuracy = 0.82 on 5-fold cross-validation (vs AUC=0.50 for the majority-class and random baselines).

The role detector (k-means with k=8 on centers of performance) yields the best silhouette score ss = 0.43; eight roles are identified: right fielder, central forward, central fielder, left fielder, left central back, right forward, right/central back, left forward.

Top-10 (most positive) feature weights are dominated by assist-related features (simple pass assist, cross assist, head pass assist, smart pass assist, high pass assist, touch assist, launch assist, key launch pass, accurate free kick, accurate shot); bottom-10 (most negative) are red-card and second-yellow fouls (hand, violent, protest, late, normal).

The average NRMSE between the overall feature weights w and competition-specific weights w^(j) is around 6%, and 16 out of 18 competitions have NRMSE < 7%; the two outliers are the European Cup 2016 (17%) and World Cup 2018 (20%) which are national-team competitions with fewer matches (51 and 64).

The distribution of player performance ratings is strongly peaked around mu = 0.39 with sigma = 0.05; ~94% of ratings lie within [mu-2sigma, mu+2sigma]; 'excellent' performances (r(u,m) > mu+2sigma) account for ~5% of the total and are unevenly distributed across players.
Only 11% of players achieve an excellent performance at least once; on average 9% of players reach excellence at least once; the maximum excellence rate is 21% for Neymar.

Validated on 211 player pairs (involving 202 distinct players) judged by three Wyscout professional scouts, PlayeRank achieves majority concordance c_maj = 68% and unanimous concordance c_una = 74% overall (vs 50% random baseline); concordance grows with ranking-distance gap, reaching c_maj=86% and c_una=91% when the gap is >=20.
Inter-Rater Agreement Rate (IRAR) between two Wyscout operators tagging the same match is approximately 0.70 overall, indicating good agreement at both event and player level.

limitations: The framework excludes goalkeepers from the analysis because they have different game rules and would require a dedicated analysis.
Soccer-logs do not include off-ball actions, so important aspects of performance such as pressing and the ability to create spaces cannot be assessed in the current version of PlayeRank.

PlayeRank's role detection is based on a player's average position via k-means clustering, which is one of several possible approaches; more sophisticated role models (e.g. heatmap- or event-direction-based) are possible but were not adopted here.
There is no objective ground-truth definition of performance quality; the team-outcome supervision is used as a proxy.
There is no consolidated and widely accepted metric for measuring performance quality in all of its facets; the authors propose PlayeRank as a candidate.
Disagreement between PlayeRank and scouts is non-trivial when compared players are close in the ranking (ranking distance < 10), where unanimous scout agreement itself is only around 58%.
open_questions: Designing more sophisticated role-detection algorithms (e.g., AI-based methods proposed in the Soccer Data Challenge) and embedding them in PlayeRank.
Designing more sophisticated feature-weighting techniques to plug into the framework.
Extending PlayeRank to work with other data sources such as video tracking data and GPS data to describe spatio-temporal trajectories and out-of-possession actions.
Plugging new performance metrics into PlayeRank's architecture and evaluating its applicability to other team sports (basketball, hockey, rugby).
Investigating alternative ways to combine the spatial-query score s(u,Q) and player rating r-bar(u,M) for the player-retrieval application.
Designing role detectors that operate at the level of fractions of a match rather than the whole match.

critic.notes: Initial batch extraction; critic pending. Unique learning-to-rank AV paradigm. Key judgment calls flagged for review: (1) family='other' chosen because PlayeRank is neither xT/EPV (state-value) nor VAEP (per-action goal-probability), but a per-action weighted-count framework with team-outcome supervision; (2) valuation_unit='action' because feature weights are per-action-type contributions even though the primary reported scalar is per-player-match; (3) framework='hybrid' (combines supervised LSVC for weights, unsupervised k-means for roles, rule-based aggregation via dot product + EWMA); (4) action_coverage.defensive_actions=true (tackles via duel-ground defending feature, interceptions via others on the ball touch interception) and set_pieces=true (free kick subtypes corner/penalty/throw-in/etc.) per Table 7; dribbles_carries=true (duel-ground dribbles and others on the ball touch acceleration/feint); off_ball_actions=false (paper explicitly states soccer-logs omit off-ball actions); goalkeeper_actions=false (paper explicitly excludes goalkeepers); (5) dataset_canonical='wyscout-private' rather than 'wyscout-public-2017-18' because the dataset covers 4 seasons of 18 competitions (~19,619 matches, 31M events) and is provided directly by Wyscout, far larger than the 2017-18 public release; only one season of ratings was later released on figshare; (6) splits string flags potential team-match-level (rather than match-level) cross-validation as a leakage concern; (7) code_release.license=null because no license is mentioned in the paper text (LICENSE on GitHub not verified offline); (8) calibration_reported=false since the paper does not report Brier/ECE or calibration curves.
